claim.why_it_matters: In the SD general format (13.3.5.1), the printed [ DEPENDING ON data-name-1 ] is an indented continuation of the IS VARYING alternative. The markdown places it flush with the alternatives, separated by blank lines like the other alternatives, so the brace reads as four alternatives and RECORD [ DEPENDING ON data-name-1 ] alone looks legal (falsely permissive syntax).

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 237 (PDF p259), 13.3.5.1: inside the RECORD brace (no choice-indicator bars) the four stacked lines are set tight. 'CONTAINS integer-1', 'IS VARYING ...', and 'CONTAINS integer-4 TO integer-5' start at one left column, and '[ DEPENDING ON data-name-1 ]' is visibly indented about 4 characters further right, which marks it as a continuation of the IS VARYING alternative. So the brace holds three alternatives. In page-259.md lines 12-18, '[ DEPENDING ON data-name-1 ]' starts at the same column as the other alternatives. Each alternative sits in its own row, with an empty spacer row between rows (rows 13 and 17 are blank, and row 15 holds only the RECORD label). The brace therefore reads as four alternatives and allows RECORD DEPENDING ON data-name-1 on its own, or without IS VARYING. The DEPENDING text is present, so nothing is missing; the defect is the lost indentation, which changes the syntax the figure describes.
